item.title: Julian Hall’s USMNT Future Hinges On One Game
item.description: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images The clock is ticking for Julian Hall. The 18-year-old Red Bulls star has a clear path to lock in his future with the USMNT, but it comes with a catch. If Hall steps onto the pitch for the United States in the upcoming Concacaf Nations League matches against Haiti, he will be permanently tied to the American side under FIFA rules. This means no going back to Poland, his other eligible nation through his mother’s heritage. USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino believes the young talent is ready . He told reporters Wednesday that Hall “fully deserves” the call-up after his performances in the previous window. He added that he did not hear Hall’s earlier comments about Poland, but that when Hall was with the team he “was really excited to play for us, for USA. That’s what is important.” The coach emphasized that commitment and performance matter more than past statements. The Rules of the Tie FIFA rules make the distinction clear for players under 21. An appearance in any official competition permanently ties a player to that national team, while friendlies alone do not. Hall has four senior caps so far, all in friendlies, so he is not yet locked in. The upcoming matches against Haiti count as official competition under CONCACAF and FIFA. Miami hosts the first match on Nov. 14, while the second occurs in Cincinnati on Nov. 17. If Hall plays in either of these, the door to Poland slams shut. He would need to file a one-time switch request, which is only possible if he hasn’t played in an official senior game yet. The window to change his mind is closing fast. A Talent Worth the Risk Pochettino is not taking chances with his roster. He brought in a wave of teenagers to test them in friendlies earlier this year, and the results were loud. During the international break spanning September and October, Hall netted three goals and recorded one assist. He earned his first senior call-up then and proved he could handle the pace. The coach sees this as a chance to blend youth with experience. Wednesday, during a video conference with reporters, Pochettino said “It’s a great opportunity,” “to mix younger [players] with experienced players.” The mix includes veterans like Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun, who are back after missing the friendly run. Hall fits right in with that new energy. Poland Still in the Mix? Back in September, Hall did not rule out the Polish national team. He told the New York Post that his international future was “definitely not solidified for me” before his first USMNT camp. He was clear about his feelings then. “I appreciate the opportunity, and I’m going to do as much as I can to make an impact, but I’m definitely still open to my Polish side,” he said. He added that he cherishes that side because his mom is from there. But the coach says actions matter more than past words. “That’s what counts. The event begins with a superhero-themed postgame drone show on May 21, followed by a bobblehead giveaway on May 22 and a kids’ cape giveaway on May 23, along with ballpark activations throughout the series. Family-focused events continue on Sundays with Pirates Family Fun Days. The Sunday lineup includes a Pregame Family Fun Zone on Federal Street and postgame Kids Run the Bases. item.title: Indiana Fever make another cut as front-office shake-up continues
item.description: Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Indiana Fever’s front-office overhaul isn’t slowing down, with the franchise quietly cutting ties with another figure. Indiana’s front-office reset has turned into pure chaos this offseason. With Kelly Krauskopf stepping down and Amber Cox shown the door, the Fever are scrambling to find a general manager while deciding against hiring a president of basketball operations. Sophie Cunningham remains a free agent, while Kelsey Mitchell just delivered an All-WNBA year alongside Caitlin Clark, but even her future is up in the air, as she also enters free agency. And it doesn’t look as if the shake-up is complete yet when it comes to the front office, as there’s been another departure behind the scenes. According to IX Sports , the Fever have moved on from basketball operations and equipment manager Kristin Moore. Kristin Moore arrived in Indiana back in early 2025 after running equipment for the Las Vegas Aces and Stanford, quickly climbing from operations coordinator to basketball ops manager. But her quiet exit after nearly two years just throws more fuel on the fire surrounding Stephanie White. Despite steering the Fever into the postseason, White’s grace period with the fanbase has evaporated, with a loud corner of the market calling for a fresh voice. The outside noise isn’t helping either, with chatter loosely floating her name for the vacant Liberty gig after Chris DeMarco got fired. item.title: Xavier soccer eyes state title with simple strategy
item.description: The Xavier boys soccer team has what seems like a pretty simple strategy. The Hawks figure if you don’t have the ball, you can’t score. It’s a high-level game of keep-away that has been effective for the Hawks, who have qualified for the WIAA state tournament for the first time since 2012. “I feel like as long as we have the ball, we have control of the game,” said senior midfielder Mauricio Laguna-Ramirez, who leads the Hawks with 15 assists. “I think that’s really what we try to do. We try to control the game, try to keep the ball as much as possible because at the end of the day, if the other team doesn’t have the ball, they don’t have any chances to score.” Xavier (14-7) is the No. 4 seed in the Division 4 semifinals and will play No. 1 seed Lake Country Lutheran (16-1-2) at 11 a.m. on Friday, Nov. 6, at Uihlein Soccer Park in Milwaukee. The Hawks are making their sixth trip to WIAA state and have been successful in their previous five appearances at state with four titles and an 8-1 all-time record. Their state titles came in Division 2 in 2003, 2004, 2006 and 2012. The Hawks have been painfully close to the state tournament in recent seasons only to fall short. They lost to Sturgeon Bay in a shootout in the sectional final last season and lost to St. Mary Catholic in the sectional final in 2023. “It’s a great accomplishment,” said junior midfielder Ethan Sharkey, who leads the Hawks with 17 goals and 35 points. “Obviously, last year, we lost in the sectional final. It’s a great opportunity that we can progress further than that. I feel like we have a great core group. We have great people coming off the bench, and I feel like we can make a run at the title this year.” Xavier has won four matches in a row and eight of its last nine after a 4-2 sectional final win over Providence Academy on Oct. 31. item.title: Green Bay Packers: Micah Parsons gets brutally honest on expectations when he returns to play after ACL injury
item.description: The Green Bay Packers are in last place in the NFC North despite having a 5-3 record. They have the best record of any last place team through eight weeks in the NFL since 1970, which is a testament to how well the division has played up to this point in the season. Truth be told, though, the Packers would be in a better position if they were not just 1-2 against their division opponents thus far in 2026. As the season hits its midway point and the weather becomes cold, Green Bay is going to be looking at making a run at a postseason spot. Fortunately, they will have All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons back soon, though he himself told fans to temper their expectations a little bit. Green Bay Packers pass rusher Micah Parsons needs to get back into game shape Green Bay Packers defensive end Micah Parsons (1) during a game against the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 12, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers defeated the Bengals 27-18. Parsons, of course, has not played yet this season as he continues to recover from the torn ACL he suffered late last year. When he first went down, the All-Pro prematurely predicted a September return. Now, we are in November and he has yet to play. This, however, is not because of any setbacks. The fact of the matter is that Parsons tore his meniscus as well. Furthermore, the Packers do not want him back on the field until he is 100% and has no risk of reinjuring that knee (remember what happened to David Bakhtiari?) While this is understood by most, it is easy to fall into the trap of thinking that Parsons will immediately be in mid-season form the second he steps onto the field for the first time. He himself told reporters that will not be the case. “I had a full lateral and medial meniscus repair, including the ACL, so when people are walking at three weeks, I’m still not weight bearing, so my quad is fully dead,” Parsons said . “I didn’t get off crutches until seven to eight weeks. So if you count that two months, I’m exactly where a nine-month (recovery) is supposed to be. So that’s why everyone’s timelines are different. I had a lot of damage done to my leg, and I think it’s a miracle that I’m even standing here today and opening up my window this early. “Am I going to be the All-Pro Micah, the person that I once was, this year? Probably not until later. I think you’ll see flashes of All-Pro Micah when I get to pass rush, and there’s gonna be times when you’re gonna be like, ‘Dang, what was Micah doing?’ There’s gonna be times that I question myself, too, like, ‘What was I doing right there?’… I’m not shying away from the possibility of my bad plays.” Fortunately, Green Bay’s pass rush has been better than many thought it would be without their All-Pro. Lukas Van Ness, Brenton Cox, Dani Dennis-Sutton, and others along the defensive front have picked up the slack and have the Packers tied for sixth in the NFL for most team sacks. item.title: Jude Bellingham joins elite company: The highest-scoring Englishmen in Champions League history
item.description: Jude Bellingham joins elite company: The highest-scoring Englishmen in Champions League history Jude Bellingham has broken into the top 10 highest-scoring Englishman in Champions League history. A brilliant back-heeled goal against AEK Athens helped Real Madrid to a 3-2 win in Greece, and saw Bellingham register his 16th goal in the Champions League. That goal has taken Bellingham into equal 10th for Champions League goals among English players, level with David Beckham . His 16th goal also equalled the mark of Belgian great Kevin De Bruyne. It was a record-breaking night for Bellingham, who became the youngest player to reach 60 Champions League appearances, aged 23 years and 128 days. He also set a new landmark as the youngest footballer ever to score in seven consecutive Champions League campaigns. In terms of English scorers in the competition, Bellingham now has Marcus Rashford, Andy Cole and Steven Gerrard in his sights as he looks to break the top five. However, he has some distance to go to catch Harry Kane . The 2026 Ballon d'Or winner has scored 58 goals and counting in the Champions League, comfortably a record among English footballers. item.title: Thursday Cannon Fodder: creeping
item.description: 03 November 2026, Thuringia, Erfurt: A heavy-duty crane is being used to lift a fir tree off a truck. A Canadian coastal fir has been erected on Erfurt's Domplatz, where it will serve as this year's large Christmas tree. The tree came from a private property in Oberhof and had been cut down on November 2 for traffic safety reasons. Its installation marked the start of the visible setup phase for the 176th Erfurt Christmas Market. Photo: Jacob Schröter/dpa (Photo by Jacob Schröter/picture alliance via Getty Images) Good Thursday morning, TSFers! Once again, it’s almost the weekend and that is always cause for celebration. It’s been a busy few weeks in my household with celebrations and guests, which is lovely, but we’ve got very little on the schedule for Saturday and Sunday and I’m thrilled. Speaking of celebrations, apparently it’s time to get ready for Christmas. At least according to Arsenal! To be fair, it’s an excellent video. I’m certain that as I watch it again, I’ll notice more references to last season and the celebrations. Colin Firth, who I think I knew supports the club, doing a nod to his Love Actually performance is fun, too. But c’mon, folks. It’s November 5th (remember, remember). There are 49 days until Christmas. The Christmas candy should not be on display in the grocery store (it’s on display in my grocery store). The Halloween decorations are still up on some of the houses in the neighborhood (like mine) and the garland and wreaths are going up. The holiday creep is too much! And I say that as someone who really enjoys the holiday time. As I write that, I remember that just because it isn’t for me doesn’t mean it isn’t for everybody. Don’t yuck someone else’s yum, Aaron. If I had my way, we’d wait a bit longer to pivot towards Christmas, but if you’re ready, go right ahead!

item.title: The one Portugal milestone Cristiano Ronaldo failed to reach as he announces retirement
item.description: Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images Cristiano Ronaldo is arguably the greatest soccer player to ever play for Portugal and has helped the national team win three trophies during his 23-year career. Despite having helped the nation reach heights they were not used to reaching, Ronaldo fell short of one achievement, which he always wanted to achieve with Portugal, and that was making 250 appearances. As he announced his retirement today, Ronaldo walks away with 234 international appearances and 146 goals, the most by any player. The announcement comes just one month after he left the Portuguese football camp in September, following controversy with head coach Jorge Jesus. “To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team,” Ronaldo said in an Instagram video. “Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone – they are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.” The Portuguese national team put out an official video on Instagram with a powerful caption that read: “A legacy that will live on forever. Thank you for everything, captain.” They also put out a statement to inform fans that a tribute was in the works for the legendary soccer player. “It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo’s immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much,” the statement read. Throughout his career, Ronaldo represented Portugal in six European Championships and won the competition once in 2016. He has also played in six World Cups and led the national team to the semi-finals in 2006. Ronaldo played in 178 competitive games and 56 friendlies throughout his career. 57 of his competitive appearances came in the World Cup and Euros. The 41-year-old has scored 25 goals in these games and helped his country become one of the leading nations in soccer. As he retires from international football, the country will now be without an icon who has carried the expectations of the Portuguese people for over two decades. Although many would say that his performances declined in the past few years, there was still an expectation of something big happening with him on the field. However, with the legend now having announced his retirement, the next generation of Portuguese talent will have to showcase that they are capable of taking the country to great heights. From the onset, Tommy Tofi, at a massive 6-foot-6, 360 pounds, possessed the tools to succeed in his first year with the Ducks (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten). Still, Lanning and offensive line coach A'lique Terry rarely go to first-year players along the interior. The only other first-year player to start for the Ducks under Lanning was current starting center Iapani Laloulu, who started the 2023 Fiesta Bowl only because Jackson Powers-Johnson opted out of the game. This is rare territory for an Oregon offensive lineman ahead of the Ducks ' biggest game of the season versus Ohio State. "It’s all been like kinda crazy," Tofi said. "Trying out different positions from left to right and just finding my rhythm." Tofi was used sparingly over the first month of the season and struggled with his assignments at times when he did get on the field. The freshman hasn't had trouble moving opposing players and creating gaps when he finds the right body, but the key has been being assignment sound. Since the second half against Nebraska on Oct. 17, Tofi has firmly held on to the left guard spot along the offensive line. He started his first game the week after against Illinois and played his best game of the season versus Northwestern last week. He said playing between Laloulu at center and veteran tackle Fox Crader has been instrumental to his success, along with his fair share of "cuss-outs." "A lot of cuss-outs from (Laloulu), (Douglas Utu) and a lot of the players," Tofi said with a smile when asked about how he's developed. "When you have four first-rounders on that D-line, that’s what helps you prepare and gets you ready for the season. Being able to go head-up with Matayo (Uiagalelei), Bear (Alexander), A’Mauri (Washington), Teitum (Tuioti), iron sharpens iron. You get better and better every day." Tofi has been part of a much-improved offensive line group that has stuck with a consistent group for the first time this season after rotating through different lineups over the first month and a half of the season. Ultimately, Lanning still wants to see more "strain" and effort from Tofi when the situation requires it. "Tommy is a guy that we’ve had a lot of confidence in from the beginning," Lanning said. "He’s got really good strength, got the ability to move people, which is huge. Now it’s about finding that extra strain. Can I strain from every play? I feel like every week that’s gotten a little better for Tommy." Alec Dietz covers University of Oregon football and women’s basketball for The Register-Guard. item.description: Colonial Country Club , home of the longest-running non-major event on the PGA Tour schedule, may not be hosting PGA Tour stars for much longer. Golfweek has learned that the Fort Worth, Texas-based private club, affectionately known as “Hogan’s Alley” for Ben Hogan’s five victories there, isn't expected to secure a place in the PGA Tour’s new Championship Series , which is scheduled to debut in 2028. Sources also say that the club likely will pass on an opportunity to participate in the Tour’s second-tier Challenger Series. Instead, Colonial, which currently hosts the Charles Schwab Challenge, could transition to PGA Tour Champions, and become the new home of the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, the season-ending playoff finale. The Tour previously said that final bids for the remaining four Championship Series events were due Sept. 30, and no decision has been made — an announcement will come at a later date. Sources say that only one tournament from the Dallas-Fort Worth area will be chosen for the Championship Series and CJ, the title sponsor for the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, has ponied up a better offer. It doesn't help that the footprint at Colonial is deemed to be maxed out and making it difficult to elevate the event the way the Tour would like to in order to generate additional revenue. More: PGA Tour overhauls competitive structure for 2028: How it works Officials view snub as 'insult' The club and Charles Schwab officials are still holding out hope that they will be selected for the Championship Series, but they are miffed that 80 years of loyalty and a sponsorship commitment that far exceeds most other companies is getting short shrift. Frustration is mounting for the club, and Schwab officials, that despite being an official marketing partner and a title sponsor on both tours, as well as the umbrella sponsor of both the season-long points race and postseason on PGA Tour Champions, they may be cast aside. They aren't thrilled with the prospect of hosting a Challenger Series event. One source said that club leadership termed being demoted after all these years as "an insult." Instead, they are believed to be weighing an offer to lean into the senior circuit and its familiar faces, many of whom are past champions and have a rich history at Colonial. The Charles Schwab Cup Playoffs consist of three events that determine the winner of the season-long title. The top 36 players in the standings following the Simmons Bank Championship advance to the Charles Schwab Cup Championship, where the player with the most cumulative points captures the Charles Schwab Cup and a share of a multimillion-dollar bonus pool. The playoff finale has been known as the Charles Schwab Cup Championship since 2003. It has been contested at Phoenix Country Club since 2017 after previously being held at Desert Mountain Club in Scottsdale, Arizona, starting in 2012. item.description: Photo credit should read BEN STANSALL/AFP via Getty Images Cristiano Ronaldo has now confirmed he has retired from the Portugal national team, just under a month after Lionel Messi played his final game for Argentina. Both players have been linked throughout their careers due to people still not being able to agree on who is the greatest of all time. That debate, even after Messi won the World Cup in 2022, is unlikely to ever be settled on a wider scale. But Ronaldo has already put forward his case for why he thinks that he is the best. During an interview, which was shared by the BBC in February 2025, Ronaldo made the case that he is ‘the most complete player to have existed’. He then suggested that while people’s taste may sway them towards liking Messi, Pele and Diego Maradona, he has not ‘seen anybody better than me’. I haven’t seen anybody better than me, and I say it from the heart.” Ronaldo ended his international career with more goals than Messi – 146 in 234 games compared to 126 in 208 games. Elsewhere, the Argentine won one World Cup and two Copa Americas while Cristiano clinched one UEFA European Championship in 2016 and has two UEFA Nations League titles. item.title: NASCAR viewership slides to historic low ahead of season finale
item.description: Credit: Greg Atkins-Imagn Images Viewership woes continue for the NASCAR Cup Series. Sunday’s Cup Series race at Martinsville averaged 1.99 million viewers on NBC. That figure is down 15% from last year’s race (2.35 million) and, more notably, marks the least-watched non-delayed NASCAR Cup Series race ever to air on broadcast television. This comes after an increase in viewership for the Cup Series last week at Talladega, albeit a modest 1%, when the series averaged 2.58 million viewers on NBC compared to 2.56 million in 2025. Prior to Talladega, Phoenix averaged just 1.29 million viewers, down 24% year-over-year. That figure practically matched the least-watched non-delayed NASCAR Cup Series race on record, with 1.29 million viewers also tuning in for the 2025 New Hampshire race. Through nine races, five Chase events have recorded year-over-year viewership increases, while four have seen declines. However, multiple double-digit drops among those four races have outweighed the gains, leading to the postseason’s overall decline in viewership. Heading into Sunday’s season finale at Homestead-Miami, The Chase is averaging 1.71 million viewers through nine races, down 3% from the same point last year (1.77 million), which was previously the least-watched postseason on record for the series. At an average of 1.71 million viewers through nine races, Sunday’s season finale at Homestead would need to average approximately 3.24 million viewers for this year’s postseason to match last year’s 1.87 million average. That would also require the highest-viewed NASCAR Cup Series season finale since 2019. Anything higher would put the 2026 Chase ahead of last year’s postseason. There were hopes that NASCAR’s reintroduction of The Chase would provide a postseason viewership boost, but that has not proven to be the case during the format’s first season back. Beyond the performance of The Chase itself, NASCAR’s continued reliance on cable television, coupled with the constant changing of races between networks throughout the season, remains an increasingly frustrating issue for fans and media observers. Haffey/Getty Images Dalton Knecht had an impressive debut with the New York Knicks weeks after the Los Angeles Lakers released him over Bronny James for their last roster spot. Knecht was the Lakers’ first-round pick in the 2024 NBA Draft while Bronny went 52nd in the same draft. Knecht earned a rotational opportunity as a rookie while Bronny focused on development, with Knecht averaging 9.1 points. After a failed trade and a downfall in form, Knecht was ultimately waived by the Lakers before opening night 2026, with Bronny winning the battle for the final roster spot. Now, Knecht might make the Lakers rue that decision. Dalton Knecht’s Knicks debut has fans abuzz with Bronny James comparisons Knecht scored 10 points and seven rebounds in his Knicks debut after signing a two-way deal with them on October 23. Lakers fans were quick to spot Knecht’s confident play and debate the team’s decision to release him and retain Bronny. “Of course it’s a mistake. JJ doesn’t know how to manage, and (Knecht) was misused after the failed trade. Why LeBum Jr. is still here is stupid,” said one fan rather harshly about Bronny and the Lakers . “He had 38 points in one game for the Lakers until he had to share with Bronny,” said a fan, also placing blame on the Lakers for prioritising Bronny . “He just wanted off the team. He got his wish and he’s balling now. Wish him nothing but good things, no hard feelings over here,” said one positive Lakers fan . “He didn’t want to be in LA. Don’t think he ever even tried to give an effort after the trade fiasco,” said another fan . “It really is the same DK. JJ was a hater and had him in solitary confinement,” were the thoughts of another fan . Bronny has looked disappointing in preseason and has scored four total points in 13 minutes over five games this season. There’s still room to develop and hopefully extract more from the 22-year-old Bronny than the 26-year-old Knecht, but it’s still a rough outcome for a Lakers team needing win-now players. Knecht averaged 7.1 points as a Laker, but his early promise never got realised after the failed trade to the Charlotte Hornets for Mark Williams in 2025. It remains to be seen if Knecht can perform consistently enough to earn a permanent roster spot in New York, but this was a great start, while Bronny continues to struggle at the NBA level in LA. item.title: Losses need not define a good team’s story
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 02: Head coach Tommy Lloyd of the Arizona Wildcats reacts in the first half of a Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame Series game against the UCLA Bruins at T-Mobile Arena on November 02, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Bruins defeated the Wildcats 84-75. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images How unfortunate that the seasons for both Arizona football and men’s basketball ended within days of each other. The former’s defeat at Texas Tech on Halloween and the latter’s loss to UCLA just two days later marked the end of the line for each program, because nothing that happens from here truly matters. Nah, that ain’t it. Losses are always disappointing and the two referenced here certainly left all of us at least bummed, if not angry. For football, the team had a golden opportunity to announce its arrival as a true contender while remaining very much in the race to win the Big 12 and reach the College Football Playoff. With hoops, the opening night loss to a hated rival offers a bad feeling for a fanbase that deep down knows a repeat of the previous season’s success is unlikely, with fears of a significant drop off lingering until proven otherwise. So yeah, those games could have gone better. The thing is, though, each team’s respective seasons could still turn out to be one that if not historical, at least worth feeling good about. It’s all about perspective. That we’re disappointed in football losing a game it was supposed to lose on the road against a team with a significantly greater roster budget because it could have won is in itself a positive. There are no moral victories when you’re trying to win a championship, but there’s a reason why the Cats were not favored to win the game. Big picture, even if the playoffs are not in the team’s future a season with 10 or more wins very much could be. Should the Wildcats get there it would put this 4 stretch among the very best in program history. The most games Arizona has ever won over a 4-year stretch is 34, and the program went into this season having won 23. Perspective. As football defensive coordinator Danny Gonzales noted this week: “Being 6-2 at the University of Arizona, and people being disappointed is freaking awesome.” It is, and while being 8-0 would be even awesomer the fact of the matter is no one really should have expected that of this year’s team, not with the schedule it was facing. That we can look back at losses to BYU and Texas Tech — both of whom are in the top 15 of the first playoff rankings — and feel like the Cats could have won each of those games shows us just how far the program has come and, unfortunately, how far it still has to go. Football is much improved and heading in the right direction, and that’s a good thing. item.title: Thursday BP: Former Giants in free agency
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 30: Kevin Gausman #12 of the Chicago Cubs pitches in the National League Wild Card game against the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on September 30, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Matt Dirksen/Chicago Cubs/Getty Images) | Getty Images MLB free agency is underway, though you wouldn’t know it by the (lack of) moves being made. It figures to be a month-long period before it goes on holiday while the owners and players bicker and negotiate and draw up a new CBA, and then free agency will return. It’s a rather uninspiring free agent class this year. Lefty ace Tarik Skubal figures to make about as much money as Elon Musk spent funding losing campaigns this year, but after that? There’s a chance that no one else clears nine figures. But there are some former Giants out there, and while most of them are likely not on the team’s radar for a potential reunion, it’s still fun keeping tabs on them. So let’s look at where the former Giants rank on two top-50 free agent lists: Fangraphs’ Ben Clemens , and ESPN’s Kile McDaniel . Second baseman Luis Arráez, who was an All-Star for the Giants in his lone season with the team this year, before being traded for a very nice haul at the deadline, is the highest-ranked former Giant, as he comes in at No. 11 on Clemens’ list and No. 12 on McDaniel’s. Unfortunately for Arráez, his performance really slowed down after the trade, as he posted an 82 wRC+ in nearly 200 plate appearances with the Philadelphia Phillies, after having a 121 mark in more than 450 plate appearances with the Giants. This seems to have hurt his standing around the league, with Fangraphs projecting him for a two-year, $38-million deal, and ESPN for a three-year, $54-million contract. Next up are a pair of righties: Kevin Gausman and Tyler Mahle. They’re back-to-back on the respective lists, albeit in different orders: Gausman is No. 15 to Mahle’s No. 16 on ESPN’s list, while Fangraphs is a little less amped, with Mahle at No. 26 and Gausman No. 27. The two publications differ quite a bit on their expectations for Gausman, who is coming off his worst ERA since 2019, though his FIP was still quite solid. Fangraphs thinks Gausman will get a modest one-year, $17-million deal, while ESPN pegs him for three years and $51 million. I’d be pretty happy with the Giants do either of those deals. While it’s easy to see the Giants targeting Gausman this offseason, they almost certainly won’t be going after Mahle, who struggled mightily on a one-year prove-it deal with San Francisco this year, before taking off after being traded to the Atlanta Braves (who promptly changed his pitch mix). That performance in Atlanta likely earned him a lot of money this winter, and Fangraphs thinks he’ll get paid $30 million over two years, while ESPN projects $49.5 million over three years.
